detail.longDescription: RE: https:// fosstodon.org/@deepfryed/11720 3975441085657 At first glance I tend to agree. However, there is a more insidious problem: LLMs amplify bias, so using them for analysis with any regularity could ruin projects, given enough time. I think that is just what they are likely to do: they will shift the code of independent projects in broken or unhealthy ways because that is what the oligarch designing the LLM prefers. The 'fixes' they offer will increasingly demand trade-offs that compromise the independence, security or viability of independent projects. The problem is, when we say 'No' to these trade-offs, the LLMs (esp. 'agentic') are poised to conduct PR offensives in the form of issues and pull requests against those of us who refuse too often. The saner approach might be to just say 'No' to all of it. Or at least to impose strict limits such as special 'LLM recon' periods lasting only days or weeks, where the devs are specially focused on dealing with LLM input and its biases. Then shut down the process at the end of the period. (No, I do not think that restricting anytime LLM use to trusted individuals will work; that is just a recipe for compromising your trusted devs.) # LLM # claude # postgres # opensource
